title: Burghley to Walsingham, Westminster 5 July 1572: name codes in a letter-book copy, BL Harley MS 260 f. 262 (DECODE R8358)

steps.what: Downloaded the two R8358 images with the DECODE cookie.
Identified the pages as Walsingham's letter-book: Burghley to Walsingham, Westminster 5 July 1572 (DECODE pages in reverse order).
Found the letter and Walsingham's 13 July reply in Digges 1655, cipher printed as figures.
Searched CSP Foreign x July 1572 (BHO pp. 140-163) for the letter or a decipherment.
Checked sibling records R8356-R8364 and Tomokiyo's Elizabethan survey for a 1572 Walsingham key.
Code [3] = the French King from context and Walsingham's reply.
Applied r8361's rule (box after a word marks a cover-name) to 'Milan [4]'; [2], [5], monogram, A, F and the run m o R d A get no value.

outcome.method_basis: The letter is Burghley to Walsingham, 5 July 1572, in Walsingham's letter-book (Harley 260), printed by Digges 1655 with the cipher unread; only code [3] = the French King was fixed from context, and no key survives for the other 14 tokens.
outcome.notes: Explained and in print; one code identified by context; the rest needs the key.

gaps.item: letter run m o R d A

prior.where: Digges 1655 prints the letter and the reply with the cipher unread; CSP Foreign x July 1572 does not calendar them

human: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.
